GoPro.note: GoPro's creation_time is not real UTC — it's the camera's raw wall-clock reading mislabeled with a 'Z' suffix (confirmed by checking its 'tmcd' timecode track, which matches creation_time almost exactly, meaning both come straight from the internal clock with no UTC conversion). That clock reads AEST (Sydney/Melbourne standard time, UTC+10), most likely because the camera was set up in Sydney before the trip and was never adjusted for AEDT daylight saving (started 2025-10-05) or for the Northern Territory's UTC+9:30.
GoPro.measured_by: Grid-searched every 15-minute offset from -30h to +30h against every real GoPro and osmo clip in E:\rushes\uluru2025 (401 GoPro, 437 osmo), counting how many GoPro clips land within 3 minutes of an osmo clip once shifted. -10h gave 156/401 matches (several within single-digit seconds, e.g. GX011407 matched within 4s); the next-best candidate offset gave only 104. Held consistently across the whole 2025-10-11..2025-10-25 trip — no sign of a mid-trip clock reset.

DJI.note: osmo's creation_time already checks out as real UTC: cross-referenced against its own filename-embedded local timestamp, e.g. DJI_20251017055310_...MP4 (05:53:10 local) vs creation_time 2025-10-16T20:53:11Z — adding NT's UTC+9:30 to the UTC value lands on 05:53:11 local, matching the filename to the second.

drone.note: Not cross-checked. Drone footage is excluded from other_bike_visible overlap logic by design (see pipeline.stage_other_bike), so its timestamp accuracy is lower-stakes — revisit if drone timing ever matters for something else.
